questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

CHRONIC
questions.solution:
The meanings of the given words are as follows:

*__**chronic: constantly recurring or (of an illness) persisting for a long time**__*

 
• *__continuing__*: without a break in continuity.
 
• *__infrequent__*: not occurring often.
 
• *__routine__*: a sequence of actions regularly followed.
 
• *__regular__*: recurring at uniform intervals.

Clearly, **'chronic'** and **'infrequent'** are words with **opposite** meanings.(**antonyms**)

Thus, option **2 **is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

The express bus __generally stops at only the major town__s on the route.

options.text: generally stop in only the major towns
generally stopped from only the major towns
generally stopping on only the major towns

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. No improvement.**

 
• The given sentence is a **routine action** and the tense used for routine action is the **present indefinite tense.**
 
• The subject in the sentence is **singular** i.e. bus, hence the **verb** used also be **singular**, so, the usage of the verb **'stops'** is correct.
 
• Hence, the given sentence is grammatically correct and needs no improvement.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

__If I does not pay__ my post-paid mobile bill by tomorrow I will probably have to pay a fine.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. If I do not pay.**

 
• The given sentence is a **conditional sentence**, hence, the first action should be in the present **indefinite tense** and the second sentence will be in the **future indefinite tense**.
 
• And in the present indefinite tense, if the subject is 'I' the helping verb i.e. do does not take **'s/es'** with it.
 
• So,** 'do not' **will be used in place of **'does not'**.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.**1.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. it.**

 
• In the given blank we need a pronoun to be used in place of **'the given sentence'**. 
 
• And the sentence is a** non-living thing** and singular.
 
• Hence, **'it'** will be used as a **pronoun** in the given blank.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.**2.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. have.**

 
• The given sentence is in **present tense**, so, option 1) i.e. **'had**' cannot be used here.
 
• And the subject is plural in the given sentence i.e. **'we'**, hence, the verb will also be plural i.e. have.
 
• Because 'has' is used for singular subjects and 'have' is used for plural subjects.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.**3.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. doesn't.**

 
• The given sentence implies that the subject does not have any pencils, hence, **'not'** will be used with the helping verb.
 
• And the subject is **singular** i.e. he, in the given sentence, hence, the helping verb will also be singular i.e. **does.**
 
• So, the correct word to fill in the given blank is **'doesn't'**.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No**.4.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. do.**

 
• The given sentence is in **present indefinite tense**, hence, the helping verb that can be used here is **'do/does'**.
 
• The subject in the given sentence is **'you'** and it takes **'do'** as a helping verb with it. 
 
• So, the correct word to use in the blank is 'do'

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No**.5.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. what.**

 
• The given sentence is an **interrogative** sentence.
 
• And 'what' is used to ask a direct question. Hence, it is the most appropriate word to use in the given blank.

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

They will not allow mobile phones in the examination hall.

options.text: Mobile phones will not be allowed in the examination hall.
Mobile phones were not allowed in the examination hall.
Mobile phones are not allowed in the examination hall.
Mobile phones are not being allowed in the examination hall.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

Future indefinite tense __**Active form**__- subject + will/shall + v1 + object + other words.

Future indefinite tense **__Passive form__**- object + will/shall + be + v3 + by + subject + other words.

Option 1 follows this rule so, the chosen option is correct.

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

The doctor told his patient, "Continue the same course of medicines for the next week."

options.text: The doctor told his patient that he may continue the same course of medicines in the following week.
The doctor told his patient to continue the same course of medicines for the following week.
The doctor told his patient for continuing the same course of medicines for the next week.
The doctor told his patient to continued the same course of medicines in the next week.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

When reported speech starts with main verb( imperative sentence) we convert this sentence in To +V1 form for making indirect speech.

Only In option 2 sentence is in construction of TO + v1 ( to continue).

So, the chosen option is correct.

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. Today, man is master of the world and he makes the animals do what he likes.

B. Others he eats; and those like the lion and the tiger, he shoots for pleasure.

C. Early man, when he first came, must have been surrounded by many huge animals, and he must have lived in fear of them.

D. Some he tames like the horse, the cow, the elephant, the dog, the cat and so many others.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. CADB.

As after reading one or two lines it can be said that this para jumble is talking about the evolution of man.

So, we must start this with the early life of a human on the earth.

Sentence C conveys this idea so, this should be the first sentence.

we have C at first position in options 2 and 4.

B & D are the sentences talking about today's man and sentence A is introducing the man today. So sentence A will follow sentence C.

Sentence B starts with others so it can not just after A as the use 'others' won't convey a clear meaning.

So we have only one choice now that Sentence D will follow sentence A and then B will come.

Thus, the correct order is CABD.
